title: Hosted API Model Catalog — Staging & Onboarding Playbook
creator: Sofia Gonzalez
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable, low-friction playbook for promoting new model variants into the Hosted API model catalog. This ticket codifies staging gates, automated validation checks, telemetry & SLO thresholds, rollback criteria, and the onboarding checklist for partner or open-model submissions.

Scope: This playbook covers models and model-variants for text generation and embeddings that will be served via Hosted API. It excludes on-prem private deployments (handled by a separate private-deploy onboarding flow). The playbook is intended for PMs, model ops engineers, runtime engineers, and Solutions/SEs onboarding customer-specific models.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-serving for a validated model variant from weeks to < 5 business days for internal teams.
- Ensure every cataloged model meets deterministic quality & safety gates before customer exposure.
- Provide clear rollback and canary policies that minimize customer impact while allowing rapid model iteration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook document published and linked from Model Catalog Confluence page; 2) Staging pipeline implemented in CI with automated checks (latency, p95, per-token cost estimate, basic safety filters); 3) A test model promoted through the playbook end-to-end with metrics captured in Console dashboards; 4) Rollback runbook validated with a tabletop exercise and documented owner list.
implementation_notes:
- Staging infra should use an isolated capacity tag (staging-variant) on Dedicated and Hosted to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
- Automated tests: latency (p50/p95), throughput under synthetic load, cost-per-million-token estimate, basic toxicity/safety classifiers, structured-output conformance tests (for generation schemas).
- Integration points: model metadata service (tags, min_sequence, tokenizer id), runtime compatibility matrix, console dashboard wiring for new metrics, and the rollout engine for canary weights.
- Owners: PM (Sofia) for playbook content, Eng runtime (Marco) for CI/workflow, MLOps (Priya) for safety checks, DX (Ethan) for onboarding docs and templates.
- Artifacts: Confluence playbook, GitHub repo for pipeline code, dashboard templates, and an onboarding checklist template in Drive.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Week 1-2): Draft playbook, align owners, implement CI smoke tests. Phase 2 (Week 3-4): Wire telemetry and dashboard templates, run two internal model promotions. Phase 3 (Week 5): Execute tabletop rollback exercise, finalize docs, and publish. Phase 4 (post-release): Collect feedback during next cycle and iterate.
- Canary policy: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over configurable windows; automatic halt if p95 latency or error rate increases by >30% and manual review required for safety flags.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Staging load leaks to production and affects customer SLAs. Mitigation: enforce capacity isolation and quota caps for staging tenants.
Risk: Automated safety classifiers produce false negatives on new model families. Mitigation: require a minimum manual safety review for first 3 promotions of an author/organization.
Risk: Telemetry gaps obscure regressions. Mitigation: mandate a telemetry checklist and block promotion without dashboard wiring.
metrics_and_success:
- Time from initial submission to catalog promotion (target < 5 business days).
- Fraction of promotions that require rollback within 30 days (target < 5%).
- Number of manual interventions during canary phase (target trending to 0 after process maturity).
- False-negative rate for safety classifier during staged promotions (tracked qualitatively initially).
